hints.title: Self-Join on Same User
hints.text: Join Purchases with itself matching the same user_id but different purchase_id.

hints.title: Day Difference Filtering
hints.text: Filter pairs of purchases where purchase_date of p2 is after or equal to p1 and within 7 days.

hints.title: Self-Join DATEDIFF Query
hints.text:
```sql
SELECT DISTINCT p1.user_id
FROM Purchases p1
JOIN Purchases p2
  ON p1.user_id = p2.user_id
 AND p1.purchase_id != p2.purchase_id
 AND p2.purchase_date >= p1.purchase_date
 AND DATEDIFF(p2.purchase_date, p1.purchase_date) <= 7
ORDER BY p1.user_id;
```

complexity.time: O(N^2) worst case per user, O(N log N) with index on (user_id, purchase_date)
variables: U: number of qualifying distinct users
complexity.notes: Filtering pairs on user_id and purchase_date bounds.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: LAG window function alone can miss pairs separated by intermediate intervening purchases.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Deduplicated user output stored in O(U) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate handles cases where multiple purchases occur within 7 days cleanly.

solutions.approach: Pandas Merge and Date Difference Filter
solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def find_valid_users(purchases: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    purchases['purchase_date'] = pd.to_datetime(purchases['purchase_date'])
    merged = purchases.merge(purchases, on='user_id', suffixes=('_1', '_2'))
    filtered = merged[(merged['purchase_id_1'] != merged['purchase_id_2']) &
                      (merged['purchase_date_2'] >= merged['purchase_date_1']) &
                      ((merged['purchase_date_2'] - merged['purchase_date_1']).dt.days <= 7)]
    unique_users = filtered[['user_id']].drop_duplicates().sort_values('user_id')
    return unique_users
